subject.title: fix(exec): require approval for OpenClaw lifecycle commands

question: Should OpenClaw permanently make gateway/daemon lifecycle mutations an explicit-approval-only class in every non-yolo exec surface, and what command-analysis ownership boundary should define that class?
rationale: This is a deliberate security and operator-workflow policy change, not a mechanical bug repair: maintainers must choose the durable set of protected lifecycle operations and the acceptable false-positive behavior.

options.title: Sponsor a narrow owned lifecycle policy
options.body: Confirm the protected lifecycle contract, move the taxonomy into the command-analysis boundary, and require final-head runtime proof before merge.

options.title: Accept the current broad classifier
options.body: Land the existing central-module taxonomy and explicitly accept its broad carrier parsing and operator confirmation behavior.

options.title: Pause for a smaller design
options.body: Defer the hard gate until a smaller shared command-analysis seam can express the policy without central parser growth.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a narrow owned lifecycle policy
recommendation.body: Confirm the protected lifecycle contract, move the taxonomy into the command-analysis boundary, and require final-head runtime proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved choice is repository-wide approval and operator policy rather than a contributor-only implementation detail.
